drug_class: Androgen biosynthesis inhibitor (hormone therapy for prostate cancer)
purpose: Abiraterone is used to treat prostate cancer that has spread to other parts of the body. It is typically used when the cancer is no longer responding well to other hormone treatments or chemotherapy. It helps slow the growth of cancer cells by lowering certain hormone levels in the body.
how_it_works: Prostate cancer cells need a hormone called testosterone to grow. Abiraterone works by blocking an enzyme called CYP17 that your body uses to make testosterone, not just in the testicles but also in the adrenal glands and even inside the tumor itself. By cutting off this testosterone supply, the drug helps slow or stop the cancer from growing.
common_side_effects: Swelling in your legs or feet, high blood pressure, low potassium levels, feeling tired, hot flashes, diarrhea, nausea, joint or muscle pain, and elevated liver enzymes. Some men also notice increased urination or urinary tract infections.
warnings: Abiraterone must always be taken with a steroid called prednisone to prevent serious hormonal side effects such as very high blood pressure, low potassium, and fluid retention. Your doctor will monitor your liver, blood pressure, and blood tests regularly. Tell your doctor right away if you notice yellowing of your skin or eyes, severe swelling, muscle weakness, or an irregular heartbeat. Women who are pregnant or could become pregnant should not handle crushed or broken tablets. Avoid taking it with food as this can raise drug levels dangerously.
typical_dosing: The usual dose of Zytiga is 1,000 mg (four 250 mg tablets) taken by mouth once a day on an EMPTY stomach — no food for at least 2 hours before and 1 hour after taking it. Yonsa (a newer form) is taken as 500 mg once daily WITH a low-fat meal. Both forms are always taken along with prednisone 5 mg twice daily as prescribed by your doctor.
